newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Air Ukraine to choose Boeing or Airbus in March.
newsitem.headline: Air Ukraine to choose Boeing or Airbus in March.

text.p: U.S. planemaker Boeing Corp and Europe's Airbus Industrie must wait until March to hear if they have won a tender to help replace state-owned Air Ukraine's fleet, company officials said on Friday.

Sergei Malyutin, Air Ukraine's acting president, told reporters at the airline's offices that a tender committee would prepare technical documents by March 1 and decide within 30 days from then on the basis of proposals from the two companies.
"Since it is Ukraine's first aviation tender we don't want any mistakes to be made," he said. "The decision is being taken at quite a high level."
The decision has been postponed several times. A senior government official said the tender would be settled this week, and the airline had said it would be finalised in mid-January.

Vice-President Vladimir Vasylenko said top officials from ministries and the aviation world, who made up the committee, were working on the tender and Boeing and Airbus had been informed of the decision.
"We are grateful to them that they understand the difficult position we are in," Malyutin said.
Malyutin could give no details on how Ukraine would organise financing, saying: "Let's wait for the results of the tender."
Talks began in March 1995 on leasing planes for existing transatlantic routes to New York and Toronto, and for planned routes to Chicago, Miami and Los Angeles.
The two men said they could give no details on current proposals from Airbus and Boeing.

Boeing had proposed selling one long-range 767 model and one mid-range 737-300. Airbus proposed leasing two long-range A-310-300 and one mid-range A-320-200 this year, and selling its newly-designed long-range A-330-200 in 1999.
Air Ukraine has nine Ilyushin-62 planes, 30 Tupolev-134 and -154 jets, 30 Yakovlev-40 and -42s, and 64 Antonov-24s. Some are not flying because of age and a fall in passenger numbers.
